taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Symphyotrichum oblongifolium and includes Texas in the native range.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — current project Hays-local source pool marks the species local/native-source material. Travis — University of Texas Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium specimen index includes Symphyotrichum oblongifolium. Bexar — San Antonio River Authority lists Symphyotrichum oblongifolium among native perennial plants for typical rain gardens in Bexar County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not add nursery/sale records as county occurrence evidence. Preserve exact county basis above unless stronger specimen/BONAP evidence supersedes it.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with growth form and foliage, not flower color: aromatic/fall aster forms a low, bushy perennial mound or colony with stiff narrow-oblong leaves and many late-season heads. Confirm the rough aromatic foliage, compact branching habit, and phyllary/head characters against taller willowleaf and panicled asters.
morphology.key_separation: Compared with S. praealtum and S. lanceolatum, S. oblongifolium is usually lower and bushier with distinctly aromatic foliage and shorter, broader-oblong leaves rather than a tall willow-leaved/panicled habit.
